findings.evidence: The same beta key accepted by GET /api/v1/chatbots/<app-A>/info initialized API MCP and returned the private B dataset ID and name from tools/list and ragflow_list_datasets. A was configured with only dataset A. No owner session/API credential was provided to the beta requests. An invalid or absent key returned application code 102; beta on ordinary GET /datasets/<B> returned HTTP 401. The normal Nginx MCP request returned HTTP 404.
findings.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: Actual document-text retrieval through MCP was attempted twice and returned isError:true: the configured local embedding endpoint refused the connection. Thus MCP metadata disclosure/scope escalation is dynamically confirmed; successful text retrieval is not. Direct API tests were inside the container and bypassed Nginx; the lab gateway blocks this MCP path.

findings.entrypoint: old API/beta credential after admin account deactivation
findings.sink_control: API/beta identity resolver and private document download
findings.evidence: After PUT /api/v1/admin/users/<synthetic-user>/activate {activate_status:off}, independent GET admin/users confirmed is_active:0. The preexisting web session returned HTTP 401; a new password login returned HTTP 200/code403 disabled. The unchanged API key still read private dataset B (HTTP 200/code0) and downloaded B's original text, including unique synthetic marker CODEX_PRIVATE_e0b02e8db69767e8ac8d, through Nginx. The unchanged beta key still read shared-app info (HTTP 200/code0) through Nginx and listed both datasets through diagnostic container-loopback MCP. No new key was issued after deactivation.
findings.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: The proven scope is the deactivated user's own previously authorized data, not arbitrary other tenants. MCP text retrieval was blocked by the offline embedding dependency. Reactivation/key-reissue policy and a remediated build were not tested; no patch was applied.
